family.description: This domain is found in many multi-domain enzymes which synthesise peptide antibiotics. This domain catalyses a condensation reaction to form peptide bonds in non- ribosomal peptide biosynthesis. It is usually found to the carboxy side of a phosphopantetheine binding domain ([pfam:PF00550]). It has been shown that mutations in the HHXXXDG motif abolish activity suggesting this is part of the active site [[cite:PUB00007135]].
family.name: Condensation domain

causal_graphs.context: C-terminal His6-tagged TycB1 variants were produced with gsp phosphopantetheinyl-transferase expression and nickel-affinity purification. The DKP assay separately preincubates each enzyme at 1 uM with 2 mM ATP and its amino-acid substrate for 3 min at 37 C, mixes equal volumes, and incubates 45 min at 37 C before extraction and HPLC-MS. Assay buffer contains 50 mM HEPES pH 8.0, 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 1 mM EDTA. The HTML gives 0.5 M phenylalanine and 0.5 mM proline before mixing; the phenylalanine unit remains unresolved rather than being silently corrected. Figure 4 uses three consecutive experiments from the same protein batch and thiolation normalization.

evidence.explanation: The quotation locates the mutant-versus-WT comparison, not the WT outcome by itself. The product Results and Figure 4 caption establish WT joint-system DKP as the normalized 100% comparator; the Methods specify the coupled assay. The orthogonal radiolabel assay includes a no-TycB1 control, which is not relabeled as an HPLC blank.
evidence.snippet: no DKP at all could be detected

evidence.explanation: Grounds the first TycB module and residue numbering without transferring the result to its other PF00668 domains or inventing the GrsA accession.

edges.mechanism: The WT joint preparation generates the d-Phe-l-Pro DKP product used as the HPLC-MS reference. This is a directly observed reconstituted-system output requiring the combined preparations and supplied substrates, not proof that TycB1 alone generates the product or that the C domain catalyzes the final cyclization.
edges.subject: joint-holo-tycb1-grsa-system

evidence.explanation: Product Results identifies R62A in the no-detected-DKP group; Figure 3 uses R62A as the representative impaired radiolabel trace. Solubility and other-domain controls limit, but do not eliminate, folding alternatives.
evidence.snippet: no DKP at all could be detected

edges.mechanism: Replacing WT TycB1 with its soluble R62A variant yields no detected DKP under the reported assay, despite retained adenylation and thiolation. The radiolabel assay also lacks the WT increase attributed to dipeptide formation. This establishes a reaction-output effect, not a directly observed structural role or proton-transfer step for Arg62.
edges.subject: tycb1-r62a-joint-system

evidence.explanation: The H147R-specific membership of the no-DKP group is reported in Results and interpreted with the other-domain controls in Discussion. No atomic mechanism is inferred from the His-to-Arg substitution.
evidence.snippet: while being still active in adenylation and thiolation activities

edges.mechanism: The soluble H147R TycB1 variant gives no detected DKP in the joint GrsA assay while retaining adenylation and thiolation. This measured loss is not a proof that His147 normally acts as a general base; coupled reactions and possible local structural effects remain unresolved.
edges.subject: tycb1-h147r-joint-system

evidence.explanation: H147V is explicitly included in the 2002 soluble-mutant and product-results groups. The absence of detectable endpoint product is kept assay-specific, not a universal zero-activity claim.
evidence.snippet: no DKP at all could be detected

edges.mechanism: The separately assayed H147V TycB1 variant also gives no detected DKP with the same GrsA partner while retaining other-domain activities. The 2002 experiment is the adopted evidence; the inaccessible 1998 precursor is not counted as an independently reviewed replication.
edges.subject: tycb1-h147v-joint-system

causal_graphs.family_mapping: TycB is UniProtKB:O30408, NCBIProtein:AAC45929.1, nucleotide AF004835, 3587 residues, sequence version 1. Current reference taxon is Brevibacillus parabrevis 54914; the sequence-linked primary operon study names historical Bacillus brevis ATCC 8185. Exact UniProt/InterPro sequence agreement places the first PF00668 interval at 9-454, containing R62 and H147. The other three PF00668 matches, including the terminal epimerization region, are not assigned this reaction. Complete construct boundaries and cloning junctions were not independently reconstructed. The paper's GrsA partner is named but not assigned an unverified accession from the two current reviewed GrsA references.
causal_graphs.limitations: DKP is an observed product of the joint coupled system; it is an indirect readout of peptide condensation followed by release/cyclization. No elementary proton transfer, isolated-domain reaction or family-wide substrate specificity is established. Retained adenylation and thiolation do not prove unchanged local C-domain folding. Absolute detection limits and independent-purification replication are not reported here. Source D151N/D151A, Y166F/Y151F and Figure 1 tycB/tycA inconsistencies remain open; no ambiguous D151 edge is adopted. Figure captions and text were inspected, not the unavailable plotted images or raw chromatograms.

record.description: This domain is found in many multi-domain enzymes which synthesise peptide antibiotics. This domain catalyses a condensation reaction to form peptide bonds in non- ribosomal peptide biosynthesis. It is usually found to the carboxy side of a phosphopantetheine binding domain ([pfam:PF00550]). It has been shown that mutations in the HHXXXDG motif abolish activity suggesting this is part of the active site [[cite:PUB00007135]].

evidence.explanation: Publisher text and captions support the reaction and three unambiguous mutant effects. D151N/D151A and Y166F/Y151F inconsistencies and the Figure 1 tycA label are retained. Neither insoluble mutants nor inhibitor sensitivity identifies a specific catalytic residue mechanism.

The separate TycC PCP-C study favors an electrostatic interpretation over general acid/base catalysis. Its abstract is a qualification and follow-up lead, not a complete review of the TycC assays or evidence transferred to TycB1.

discussions.notes: Obtain accessible original figures, full clone descriptions and raw product/normalization evidence; expand other family contexts separately. The 1998 JBC PDF and direct publisher figure downloads were unavailable. Other substrates, epimerization/cyclization subfamilies and later studies remain incompletely covered. Imported identity and classification are unchanged.
discussions.prompt: Resolve TycB1 construct and assay ambiguities before assigning an elementary condensation mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Coupled reaction output and domain-localized mutations support a scoped biochemical graph, but not a universal histidine proton-transfer step. Exact fusion sequences, GrsA accession, phenylalanine units and inconsistent D151 labels remain unresolved.
